what_happened: All three countermodel grades, both transfer theorems, and a language-generic CountermodelEntry type compile-verified in two probe files on the first/second attempt: the gate theorem repackaged on explicit branch data (no kernel tableau rebuild) gives a kernel-checked gated-tableau entry with axioms [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound].

The plan's Lean Challenge Statements block cross-validated against the Goals identifier set and COMPILED against the project's own toolchain on the first attempt (lean-challenge-snapshot.sh 973 . --dry-run --compile, exit 0), confirming every pinned signature's namespaces resolve (PointTruth, GenericValidIn, Branch, TimeOrdering, ofFormula) before any implementation dispatch runs. Compile-checking the Challenge block at plan time is cheap and catches the namespace errors the research report itself hit twice.

All 8 non-final phases' first-draft Tier Justification lines claimed the no-suite sentinel, which validate-artifact.sh rejected as a false claim. Root cause measured: plan-file-scope-harvest.sh auto-appends typst/generated/status.typ to EVERY phase carrying a .lean edit (this repo declares it a coupled generated surface), and that path maps to two real suites (test-plan-file-scope-harvest.sh, test-validate-artifact.sh). So a Lean-repo phase's selector output is always MIXED even when every named path maps to nothing. Corrected all 8 to name the two real suites; plan now validates with 0 warnings.

Backtick-delimited identifier lists written as annotation prose inside a Files to modify entry (e.g. 'new: `A`, `B`, `C`') are read by validate-artifact.sh as a comma-joined second path and warned on in 3 phases. Fix: annotation prose in Files to modify blocks carries no backticks at all. Worth knowing for any plan whose deliverables are named declarations.
